title: File the annual unclaimed property holder report (Connecticut)
description: Businesses holding property that has gone unclaimed — uncashed payroll or vendor checks, customer credits and refunds, unused gift cards, deposits — must report and turn it over to the state each year, after sending the owner a due diligence notice before the deadline. The annual report and payment are due March 31 for general property. A negative report is required even when the business holds nothing. The directory page says March 30; other sources say March 31. Which state's law applies depends on the owner's last known address, or the business's state of incorporation when there is none, so a business can owe reports to several states.

title: Classify contractors with the ABC test for unemployment and wage law (Connecticut)
description: Connecticut applies the ABC test to unemployment insurance and, per one policy group's table, wage and hour rules; a worker who fails any prong is an employee.

title: Notify residents and regulators of a data breach within 60 days (Connecticut)
description: If personal information of residents of the state is acquired without authorization, notify affected residents within 60 days of discovering the breach (Conn. Gen. Stat. 36a-701b). This is an event-driven duty, so it has no calendar date. Sources in the PR describe the state's rule in different words; check the statute for the exact trigger and content of the notice.
